relevance.rationale: JOIN CONFIRMED, with a wrinkle resolved in the join's favour: the PDF is an arXiv posting that describes itself on p.1 as a corrected version of the journal article the registered entry records, so posting and entry are the same work and the seeded key is right. Single citation site: folio/quantum-observable-universe/lean/QOU/BraidKnot/KeystoneSelfDualSpectralNarrowing.lean:59, which labels it 'self-reciprocal q-Hankel transform on E_q(2)'. The substantive half is CORRECT: the transform pair on pp.9-10 uses the same third-q-Bessel kernel in both directions, so the transform is its own inverse, and it degenerates to the classical Hankel pair as q -> 1. MINOR OVER-ATTRIBUTION: 'on E_q(2)' is not the document's framing. It says (p.1 and §1) that its results are only implicit in the quantum-group context of another paper, whose authors gave the interpretation on the quantum group of plane motions; this document itself works in q-special-function terms and never states the transform on that quantum group. The Lean line compresses the other authors' setting into this citation. The citation is load-bearing (self-reciprocality is exactly the property the module's S^4 = 1 narrowing formalizes categorically); only the venue label needs softening.

keyResults.statement: A q-Hankel transform pair with the same third-q-Bessel kernel in both directions, hence self-reciprocal, degenerating to the classical Hankel pair as q -> 1.
keyResults.useForFolio: The analytic prototype of the self-reciprocality the keystone narrowing formalizes as S^4 = 1, and the reason a free-scale q-Bessel family is a duality template rather than a zero-dof node screen.

proposedActions.rationale: Soften the 'on E_q(2)' clause at KeystoneSelfDualSpectralNarrowing.lean:59: the self-reciprocal pair is this document's, but the quantum-group-of-plane-motions setting belongs to the paper it cites rather than to it.
